entries.subject: Radius and orbit adopted from the published record
entries.finding: Radius 1.17 ± 0.08 Earth radii from Torres et al. 2015 (ApJ 800, 99 (2015); arXiv:1501.01101), at 6378.137 km per Earth radius. No mass is measured, so no gravitational parameter is adopted. A sphere: no oblateness is measured. Orbit: Torres et al. 2015 (ApJ 800, 99 (2015); arXiv:1501.01101), Table 8, column KOI-0571.05: 129.9441 d Inclination 89.96 degrees and a/R* = 178 (+65/-21) from Torres et al. (2015), Table 8. Eccentricity is set to 0: a circular display approximation, not an orbital solution. Torres et al. 2015, Table 8, column KOI-0571.05: tau = BJD_UTC 2455789.4940 (the paper gives the time in UTC, not TDB; the difference of about a minute is not applied).

entries.subject: Whether the transit signal is a planet
entries.finding: Planet or false alarm: Torres et al. (2015) validated it. Burke et al. (2019): no longer meets the 1% criterion, planet probability 96%; Robnik & Seljak (2025): false-alarm probability 20%, not validated. The dispute is stated on the page.
